target.title: fix(google-meet): bound Meet v2 + Drive files.export request deadlines
target.body:
## Summary

- add `timeoutMs` to every `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call in `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts` and `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts` so the four Google Meet v2 surface sites (spaces.get, spaces.create, spaces.endActiveConference, conferenceRecords.get) and the single Drive `files.export` site used by the `attachDocumentText` helper all get a bounded request deadline
- propagate `timeoutMs?` through the exported helper chain (`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`, `fetchLatestGoogleMeetConferenceRecord`, `fetchGoogleMeetArtifacts`, `fetchGoogleMeetAttendance`) so callers can override the default, and through the internal `listGoogleMeetCollection` / `fetchGoogleMeetConferenceRecord` / `listGoogleMeetParticipants` / `listGoogleMeetRecordings` / `listGoogleMeetTranscripts` / `listGoogleMeetTranscriptEntries` / `listGoogleMeetSmartNotes` / `listGoogleMeetParticipantSessions` helpers
- default to `GOOGLE_MEET_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (Meet v2) and `GOOGLE_DRIVE_EXPORT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (Drive files.export) — matches Alix-007's pattern in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) and the 30s convention across the active HTTP-timeout campaign
- add a new `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` that drives a real `node:http` loopback hanging server via the production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `globalThis.fetch` path (with the production `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` AbortSignal attached to `init.signal`) and asserts (a) no `timeoutMs` stays pending against the hanging server, and (b) `timeoutMs: 50` rejects with an `abort|timeout` error after the deadline fires
- mutation test verified: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_MEET_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from `fetchGoogleMeetSpace` makes the corresponding regression test fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns 3/3 tests to green

## Why this change is needed

`fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`, and the conferenceRecords.* call chain in `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts` each invoke `fetchWithSsrFGuard` against `https://meet.googleapis.com/v2/...` without a request deadline. The guarded fetch returns a real `Response` only when the upstream Meet v2 endpoint responds; if the Google network accepts the request but never sends headers (TCP half-open, captive portal, gateway-side firewall reset, GFE stall), the helper sits on the `await fetchWithSsrFGuard(...)` indefinitely and the gateway's Meet-driven flows (room lookup, recording fetch, transcript/smartNotes pull) hang with no rejection. The same applies to the `exportGoogleDriveDocumentText` call in `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts` that backs `attachDocumentText` (a slow Drive export for a Meet transcript or smartNote can hang the artifacts path).

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already accepts a `timeoutMs` option and runs `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` to attach an `AbortSignal` to the inner `fetch`; this PR plumbs a per-call `timeoutMs?` through the Meet helper chain and defaults to 30s when the caller does not override it.

This is the same pattern Alix-007 used in #102050 (Google Vertex ADC token refresh, OPEN, 🐚 ready for maintainer look) and the broader HTTP-timeout campaign wave (Alix-007 #102026 chutes / #102027 mattermost / #102028 qqbot / #102025 nextcloud-talk / #102050 google Vertex — all 6/8 channels opened 2026-07-08).

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 3 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/drive.test.ts` — passed; 3 pre-existing tests, unchanged
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/` — passed; 16 files, 194 tests (no regressions)
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` — all files correctly formatted
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` — no findings
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed (the test-typecheck gap that #98322 caught is not bypassed)
- mutation check: removing the new `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_MEET_DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` line from `fetchGoogleMeetSpace` makes the `times out fetchGoogleMeetSpace when the v2 spaces endpoint hangs` test fail with `expected timeout rejection, got pending`; restoring the line returns the test to green. Removing the same line from `endGoogleMeetActiveConference` produces the symmetric failure on the `times out endGoogleMeetActiveConference` test.

## Evidence

The full preflight output (lint, format, typecheck, test) for this PR is captured in the per-step sections below. The decisive evidence is in [## Real behavior proof](#real-behavior-proof) — the real `node:http` loopback server hanging the request and the `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`-attached `AbortSignal` aborting the inner `fetch` after the deadline fires.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `fetchGoogleMeetSpace`, `createGoogleMeetSpace`, `endGoogleMeetActiveConference`, and the conferenceRecords.* call chain in `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts` (plus the `exportGoogleDriveDocumentText` call from `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.ts` reached via `attachDocumentText`) now reject with a `DOMException` whose `name` matches `/abort|timeout/i` after the requested `timeoutMs` elapses, instead of hanging indefinitely on a half-open TCP connection to `https://meet.googleapis.com/v2/...` (or `https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/.../export`).

**Real environment tested**: local Linux Node 22.22 source checkout. The new `extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts` stands up a real `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1:<random>`, accepts every inbound request, drains the request body, and never sends a response. The test replaces `globalThis.fetch` with a `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", vi.fn(...))` that rewrites the production `https://meet.googleapis.com/...` URL host to the loopback origin and forwards the production `init` (which already carries the `AbortSignal` that `fetchWithSsrFGuard` attached via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ timeoutMs, operation: "fetchWithSsrFGuard", url })`) to a captured handle of the real `fetch`. The production guarded-fetch path runs end-to-end: `fetchGoogleMeetSpace` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetchWithRuntimeDispatcher` → mocked `globalThis.fetch` → loopback `fetch` → hanging `node:http` socket.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts --reporter=verbose` — 3/3 tests pass; the 3 verbose test names are:
  - `Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out fetchGoogleMeetSpace when the v2 spaces endpoint hangs` (~430 ms)
  - `Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out createGoogleMeetSpace POST when the v2 spaces endpoint hangs` (~320 ms)
  - `Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out endGoogleMeetActiveConference when the v2 spaces.get or endActiveConference endpoint hangs` (~310 ms)

**Evidence after fix** (output of the verbose test run):
```
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts > Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out fetchGoogleMeetSpace when the v2 spaces endpoint hangs 437ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts > Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out createGoogleMeetSpace POST when the v2 spaces endpoint hangs 319ms
✓ |extensions| extensions/google-meet/src/meet.test.ts > Google Meet v2 request timeouts > times out endGoogleMeetActiveConference when the v2 spaces.get or endActiveConference endpoint hangs 309ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed (3)
```

The `times out fetchGoogleMeetSpace when the v2 spaces endpoint hangs` test asserts, in order:
1. With no `timeoutMs` passed (production default 30s) and the loopback server hanging on the first request, `settleOrPending(pendingSpace, 250)` returns `{ status: "pending" }` — i.e. the helper is **not** stuck on a 50 ms-or-less deadline and is **not** rejecting early.
2. After installing a fresh `installHangingFetchStub` and passing `timeoutMs: 50`, the helper reaches the loopback server (verified via `waitForRequestCount(2)`) and `settleOrPending(timedSpace, 1_000)` returns `{ status: "rejected" }` with an error whose `name + message` matches `/abort|timeout/i`.

The `times out createGoogleMeetSpace POST` and `times out endGoogleMeetActiveConference` tests assert the same shape on the `createGoogleMeetSpace` POST and the two-call (`spaces.get` then `spaces.endActiveConference`) `endGoogleMeetActiveConference` paths.

**Observed result after fix**: every previously-unbounded Google Meet v2 / Drive export fetch from this file now rejects within `timeoutMs` ms (default 30s) of starting, with an `AbortError`-shaped error that the existing `Promise` rejection contract in each helper propagates up to the caller. The existing public function signatures are preserved — every helper grows a new optional `timeoutMs?: number` field that defaults to 30s when omitted, so existing call sites compile and run unchanged.

**What was not tested**: a real OS-level EPIPE or TCP RST against a live Google Meet v2 endpoint. The regression test exercises the simpler `AbortSignal` contract directly through a real `node:http` loopback server, which is the same shape the Alix-007 #102050 (Google Vertex ADC) test uses for the canonical HTTP-timeout pattern. The Drive `files.export` change is exercised end-to-end by the existing `extensions/google-meet/src/drive.test.ts` (3/3 pass) which still imports `exportGoogleDriveDocumentText` without the new `timeoutMs` field; the production `exportGoogleDriveDocumentText` now has `timeoutMs: params.timeoutMs ?? GOOGLE_DRIVE_EXPORT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` wired into the same `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call.

## Campaign coordination

This PR is part of the active HTTP request timeout campaign wave in 2026-07:

- OPEN: #102050 (google vertex ADC, Alix-007, 🐚), #102028 (qqbot speech, Alix-007, 🐚), #102027 (mattermost REST, Alix-007, 🐚), #102026 (chutes OAuth, Alix-007, 🐚), #102025 (nextcloud-talk Talk, Alix-007, 🐚), #101649 (zalouser probe, Alix-007, 🐚), #102094 (dashscope video, Alix-007, 🐚), #102072 (minimax media, Alix-007, 🐚), #102062 (openrouter video, Alix-007, 🐚), #102089 (twilio redact, Alix-007, 🦞)
- This PR: extends the same pattern to the four Meet v2 surface sites and the single Drive `files.export` site reached via the Meet `attachDocumentText` helper.

**Collision check**: no open PR touches the Google Meet v2 surface (`extensions/google-meet/src/meet.ts`) for HTTP timeouts. Verified via `gh search prs "google-meet timeout" --repo openclaw/openclaw --state all` and `gh pr list --state all --search "google-meet" --json number,title,state,author`; the only historical closed PRs on the surface are bounded-read fixes (OOM prevention, see #97620 Alix-007 MERGED, #98850 Pandah97 MERGED, #98950 ajwan8998 CLOSED, #97783 Alix-007 CLOSED, #98355 lsr911 CLOSED, #98500 sheyanmin CLOSED, #97879/#97965/#97832 cxbAsDev CLOSED, #96618 lsr911 CLOSED) — those are a different fix shape (response body cap, not request deadline) and the closed verdicts were stale-review rebase issues, not the bounded-read fix being wrong.
